GlobalForge Equipment Corp. - Q4 FY2023 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the GlobalForge Equipment Corp. Q4 FY2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GlobalForge Equipment Corp.'s results for the Q4 FY2023. Joining me on today's call are Maria Voss, Chief Executive Officer; Kevin Hargrove, Chief Financial Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Maria Voss.

Maria Voss (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on GlobalForge Equipment Corp.'s performance for the Q4 FY2023. We've made significant progress on several fronts, delivering our strongest quarterly results in over five years. Total revenue reached $2.68 billion, up a robust 14.2% year-over-year, outpacing the industrial equipment sector's 6-7% growth. This momentum carried through the full year with $10.47 billion in consolidated revenue, a 9.8% increase.

We saw strong demand trends across key end markets—construction benefiting from U.S. infrastructure spending, mining fueled by commodity strength, agriculture holding steady amid precision upgrades, and manufacturing surging on reshoring. Our aftermarket parts and services grew 8.9% to $1.13 billion in the quarter, representing 42% of revenue with record attachment rates thanks to our ForgeLink IoT platform.

Inventory levels are well-controlled at $1.42 billion, with days inventory outstanding at 82 days, reflecting smart management strategies like AI forecasting and vendor-managed inventory. Our backlog hit a record $7.8 billion, up 28% year-over-year, providing clear visibility with strong conversion expected over the next 12-24 months.

Cost reduction initiatives generated $185 million in savings for the year, expanding gross margins by 420 basis points through supply chain optimization, manufacturing productivity gains, and value engineering. Looking ahead, we're guiding Q1 FY2024 revenue to $2.55-2.65 billion and full-year FY2024 to $11.2-11.6 billion, implying 7-11% growth.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Kevin Hargrove to provide more detail on our financial results.

Kevin Hargrove (CFO):
Thank you, Maria. Turning to our financial performance, GlobalForge Equipment Corp. reported $2.68 billion in revenue for the Q4 FY2023, representing a 14.2% increase year-over-year from $2.35 billion in Q4 FY2022. This exceeded our guidance midpoint by 3% and marked our strongest quarterly performance in over five years. On a full-year basis, consolidated revenue climbed to $10.47 billion, up 9.8% from $9.54 billion in FY2022, outpacing the broader industrial equipment sector's roughly 6-7% growth per S&P Global data. This was driven by our focus on high-margin automation and electrification products amid a recovering capex cycle.

Breaking it down by segment, our core areas—Equipment Sales, Parts & Services, and Engineered Systems—each contributed meaningfully, with favorable mix shifts boosting overall margins. Equipment Sales, accounting for 58% of Q4 revenue at $1.55 billion, grew 18.7% year-over-year, fueled by a 12% volume increase and 5% pricing realization. Average selling prices held firm despite inflationary headwinds on steel and components. Key wins included shipments of our next-gen Nexus-4000 series CNC machining centers, which saw 25% demand growth in automotive OEMs re-shoring production lines, and ramped deliveries of electric hydraulic presses for battery manufacturing, capturing share in the EV supply chain through partnerships similar to those with Tesla's Gigafactory expansions and LG Energy Solutions.

Parts & Services, our highest-margin segment at 42% of Q4 mix and $1.13 billion in revenue, delivered 8.9% YoY growth. Attachment rates hit a record 28% on new equipment, up from 24% last year, thanks to our ForgeLink IoT platform, now installed on over 65% of our active fleet. This predictive maintenance system reduced unplanned downtime by 22% for customers and drove recurring service revenue, with utilization rates in our installed base averaging 82%, supported by strong aftermarket demand for precision tooling and retrofit kits. In Q3 alone, aftermarket parts and services revenue grew 18% year-over-year to $162 million, marking our 11th straight quarter of double-digit growth, outpacing overall company growth of 12%. Trailing 12-month contribution to total revenue reached 29%, up from 26% a year ago, and we're on track for $650 million full-year, over 30% of projected $2.1 billion total revenue with 16-17% growth. Our global fleet exceeds 85,000 units, averaging 7.2 years in North America, driving ARPU to $7,800 per unit. North America contributed 52% with 22% growth, EMEA 26% at 14%, and APAC 22% at 12%, powered by ApexConnect IoT with edge AI reducing failures and Uptime-as-a-Service bundles achieving 95% renewals.

Engineered Systems, 5-10% of total at $180 million in Q4 up 22% YoY, benefited from large project bookings in semiconductor fab automation, including turnkey assembly line integrations for Intel's Ohio fab and TSMC's Arizona expansion using our modular robotic palletizers.

Regionally, performance was balanced: North America at 52% or $1.39 billion, up 17% on IIJA and CHIPS Act infrastructure; EMEA 28% or $750 million, +12% with wind turbine demand at Siemens Gamesa; Asia-Pacific 18% or $480 million, +9% via localized production in Pune and Shanghai, gaining to 14% market share in material handling; Rest of World 2% with Latin American mining gains.

Pricing discipline realized 4.8% net price, countering 6-8% raw material inflation via pass-throughs and VAVE. Volume leverage came from orders up 16% to $2.9 billion, pushing 12-month backlog to $7.8 billion, up 28% YoY—75% of FY2024 expected revenue, diversified across cycles versus Komatsu's longer mining backlog. Our $250 million FY2023 R&D—7% of sales above industry 5%—yielded AI-optimized Nexus Servo Drives cutting energy 30%, with electrification at 22% of mix up from 12%, and ForgeLink 2.0 integrating with Siemens MindSphere and Rockwell FactoryTalk.

Our 'Forge Forward' initiative prioritizes high-tech sustainable equipment, gaining 150 bps market share to 9.5% in automation per Gartner, with 42% win rates. FX shaved 1.2% off growth, and non-residential construction softens, but our 15% construction exposure limits risk versus peers.

Before turning to outlook, a note on inventory: Ending inventory stood at $1.42 billion, up 8% sequentially but flat YoY, with DIO at 82 days versus industry 95 days average like Caterpillar's 98 or Deere's 102. Turns at 4.5x TTM, up from 4.1x, with 96% fill rates. Raw materials $640 million up 12% QoQ on pre-buys; finished goods $426 million up 5%; WIP $354 million down 3% YoY via flow cells cutting cycles to 38 days. North America 55% at $780 million up 10%; Europe 25% flat; APAC 15% down 5%; LatAm up 15%. SAP S/4HANA AI cut forecast error to 14%; VMI shifted $120 million off balance sheet covering 28% BOM; ABC/XYZ culled 1,200 SKUs, obsolescence at 1.2%; digital twins in Oracle SCM shaved DIO 6 days locally; safety stock at 98% service level.

Our backlog at quarter-end was $7.8 billion overall, but refining to Q2-like detail for visibility: total $8.4 billion equivalent in strength, up 18% YoY and 5% sequentially—fifth straight quarter expansion. Aerospace & Defense 42% $3.5B up 25%; Automotive 28% $2.4B +12%; Renewables 18% $1.5B +35%; Construction & Mining 12% $1.0B flat YoY up seq. North America 65% $5.5B +22%; EMEA 20% $1.7B +10%; APAC 15% $1.2B +5%. Conversion: 62% within 12 months, 85% in 24; granularly 33% 0-6 months $2.8B +20%; 29% 7-12 $2.4B +15%; 27% 13-24 $2.3B +18%; 11% 25+ $0.9B +12%. Digital twin ERP with Siemens Xcelerator cut lead times 15%; Industry 4.0 to 92% utilization; electrified lines 25% of backlog at premium pricing; book-to-bill 1.2x.

Cost reduction initiatives delivered $185 million in FY2023 savings, exceeding $150 million target by 23%, expanding gross margins 420 bps to 32.8% and EBITDA 250 bps to 18.2%. Supply chain (45% $83M): suppliers down 22% to 940, 12% materials savings; nearshoring 35% steel to Mexico/U.S. cut freight $22M; HSLA substitutes 9% cheaper; VMI $12M. Manufacturing (30% $56M): OEE to 91% with 450 cobots saving $28M labor; ApexPredict IoT cut downtime 32% $14M; energy retrofits $9M. SG&A (15% $28M): 4.2% headcount cut $18M; DCs consolidated $6M; cloud $4M. Product (10% $18M): DFM 40% tooling cut; modularization. Impact: COGS down 8.7% sales %; EBITDA +$93M net; EPS $1.42 +22%; FCF $420M. Gross margin +420 bps (supply 280, mfg 110); EBITDA +250 bps.

Demand trends: Construction 35% orders +12% book-to-bill 1.25x, IIJA highway +18%, non-res data centers +22%; Mining 28% +22% copper $4.50/lb CapEx $12B, autonomous +40%; Ag 20% -5% but precision +18%, fleet age 8.5 yrs; Manufacturing 17% +9% reshoring fabs/EV +25%. Total orders $1.6B +11%, backlog $5.2B +25%, aftermarket 40% +14%.

Looking ahead, Q1 FY2024 revenue guided $2.55-2.65 billion, sequential 5-11% up, YoY 12-17%. Heavy Machinery $620-650M +3% pricing; Precision Automation $480-500M +25% bookings; Aftermarket $250-270M high-single digits. North America ~55% +20%; EMEA flat-5%; APAC headwinds offset India. Full FY2024 raised to $11.2-11.6 billion, 7-11% up, organic 10-13% + pricing 2-3; aftermarket +18%; $500M contracts; $50M FX drag. Backlog 90% 12 months, $300M capex vertical integration.

Gross margin {28.5% say}, operating income strong, net income solid, EPS ahead. Committed to strong balance sheet and cash flow.

Now, I will hand over to Sarah Chen, COO, for an operational update.

Sarah Chen (COO):
Thank you, Kevin. Operationally, we've been focused on optimizing our supply chain, improving manufacturing efficiency, and enhancing customer service across our global plants. Leveraging data analytics from SAP S/4HANA and digital twins, we've identified key improvements, driving OEE to 91% and reducing WIP cycles. We're investing in employee training, upskilling 2,500 associates in PLC programming with Rockwell partners, building a skilled workforce for Industry 4.0. Supply chain resilience via multi-sourcing and VMI ensures 96% on-time delivery, while LEAN initiatives and cobot deployments cut labor and defects. Customer service levels at 96%, with ForgeLink boosting utilization to 85%.

And I will turn the call over to our CTO, Dr. Raj Patel, for an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Raj Patel (CTO):
Thank you, Sarah. We are committed to driving innovation and developing cutting-edge solutions for our customers. Our $250 million R&D investment in FY2023—7% of sales—targets artificial intelligence, machine learning, and IoT. We're advancing predictive maintenance via ForgeLink and ApexConnect on 40,000+ assets, cutting downtime 28-32% with edge AI anomaly detection. New Nexus-4000 CNCs and AI-optimized servo drives reduce energy 30%, electrified products now 22% mix with hybrid forklifts and electric welders growing triple-digits. Digital twins with Siemens Xcelerator and integrations with MindSphere/FactoryTalk enable 15% faster lead times and 92% fab utilization. Our electrified EQ-500 skid steers and HydroMax drives command premiums, supporting ESG and autonomy for mining/construction. The new Nexus Servo Drives platform is exceeding expectations, with 30% energy savings driving 25% adoption in renewables and semiconductors.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you discuss the trends you are seeing in automation spending?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thanks for the question, John. Automation spending remains robust, tied to reshoring, labor shortages, and Industry 4.0. In manufacturing, U.S. factory output up 4.2% ISM, with CHIPS Act fabs like Intel Ohio and TSMC Arizona driving 25% YoY bookings for our AI-optimized CNCs and robotic palletizers. Automotive EV lines for Ford/Stellantis added $2.4B backlog. Renewables surged 35% with Vestas/GE Vernova wind gearboxes. We're seeing 1.2x book-to-bill, with digital twin ERP and IoT upgrades boosting throughput 15%. R&D focus on AI paths and edge computing positions us for 25% CAGR factory automation per McKinsey, gaining share versus Fanuc/Siemens.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Johnson (JPMorgan):
What is your strategy for managing inflation and rising input costs?

Kevin Hargrove:
Great question, Emily. Inflation on steel up 15% YTD, aluminum tariffs, energy +25% Europe—we countered with $185M savings via four pillars. Supply chain: nearshored 35% steel saving $22M freight, HSLA subs 9%, VMI $12M, hedged steel at $650/ton. Manufacturing: cobots 22% labor cut, IoT predictive 32% downtime reduction $14M, VFDs 19% energy save. SG&A: headcount opt $18M, DC consol $6M. Product: DFM 40% tooling, modularization. Net 420 bps gross margin expansion to 32.8%, 93% savings to EBITDA. Locked 80% 2025 inputs, targeting $220M FY24 savings, gross to 34%+.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Lee (Morgan Stanley):
Can you provide an update on your efforts to reduce your carbon footprint?

Maria Voss:
Absolutely, Mike. Sustainability is core to Forge Forward. Electrification at 22% mix cuts Scope 1/2 emissions 18%, with EQ-500 series and HydroMax reducing fuel 25%, aiding EU ETS/CBAM compliance. Energy retrofits dropped kWh/ton 19%, solar microgrids in India. Reman parts ISO 14001 up 35% EMEA. R&D yields 30% energy savings in servo drives. Wind/renewables backlog $1.5B, IRA tailwinds. Down 18% emissions YTD, targeting vertical rare earths for EV motors, aligning with Green Deal and IIJA for long-term de-risking.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Maria Voss:
Thank you for your questions and your interest in GlobalForge Equipment Corp. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
